description: Arpanaei, Farhad and colleagues document this resource in the B5G-OPEN community. 6D-MAN is explicitly described as a developed planner for heterogeneous multilayer metro networks. It simulates multi-homed edge-to-core routing, modulation selection and spectrum assignment for multiband and multifibre transmission. Coverage includes 100–400 Gb/s flexible transponders on a 50-GHz grid and selective C+L migration in reference metropolitan networks. Companion Telefónica studies preserve their operator-specific application. Ten-year cost and fibre-deployment results are scenario outputs. Code availability, package interfaces and reproduction of the claimed savings are not established. Zenodo provides the descriptive publication with open access; its stated licence is cc-by-4.0. Its publication licence does not establish a code licence or source-code availability. A limitation is that the native metadata do not establish all implementation settings, uncertainty bounds or independent reproducibility. Only descriptive metadata were inspected. Related records and companion papers retain their source-defined roles; they do not imply independent measurements.
